artworks.title: Pygmalion and Galatea
artworks.description: Gérôme's Cypriot sculptor kissing life into ivory — the academic image that fixed Pygmalion for the salon age.

artworks.title: Pygmalion and Galatea
artworks.description: Girodet's Louvre canvas catches the instant marble softens into flesh: Cupid's torch lights Galatea as Pygmalion kneels in astonishment. Neoclassical polish for Ovid's sculptor who loved his own work into life.

artworks.title: Pygmalion Praying Venus to Animate His Statue
artworks.description: Regnault's Origin of Sculpture shows Pygmalion before Venus, begging life for the ivory maiden — the prayer that precedes the kiss. Painted for the French crown and still at Versailles.

artworks.title: Pygmalion and the Image: The Soul Attains
artworks.description: The last panel of Burne-Jones' Birmingham Pygmalion series: Galatea steps living from the pedestal into the sculptor's arms. Pre-Raphaelite quiet after the prayer, the myth fulfilled in soft light.

artworks.title: Pygmalion carves his ivory maiden (Roman de la Rose)
artworks.description: Roman de la Rose (NLW MS 5016D, f. 130r): Pygmalion at work on the statue he will fall in love with, the story Jean de Meun retells at length near the end of the poem.

films.title: My Fair Lady
films.description: Higgins as Pygmalion — Audrey Hepburn's Eliza the living statue speech remakes.

music.title: My Fair Lady
music.description: Broadway's most famous Pygmalion — the sculptor myth as musical theatre of class and voice.

popCulture.title: Pygmalion (play)
popCulture.creator: George Bernard Shaw
popCulture.description: Shaw borrowed the sculptor's name for Higgins — creation as social engineering, Galatea as Eliza.
